extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant peer reviewers and scientific review officers (first‑level peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for scientists serving as NIH first‑level peer reviewers and scientific review officers on evaluating grant applications, conducting study section meetings, scoring, writing critiques, and complying with integrity/conflict rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of first level peer reviewers is to assess the overall impact that a proposed project will likely have on the biomedical research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should form an overall-impact judgment of the likelihood the project will have a sustained, powerful influence on the research field; the final 'overall impact score' for an application is determined by the entire review panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate using FOA-established review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must evaluate applications using the criteria established in the notice of funding opportunity to which an application(s) was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the specific review criteria published in the applicable FOA; additional guidance for how to evaluate individual criteria is available through standard reviewer guidance documents such as 'Peer Review Criteria and Considerations' and 'Review Criteria Information'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess human subjects, vertebrate animals, and biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of review meetings, the Scientific Review Group will discuss any concerns with the use of human subjects, vertebrate animals, and/or biohazards within applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and surface ethical, regulatory, or safety concerns related to human subjects protections, animal welfare, or biohazard containment during the review discussion and in written critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring process: preliminary and final ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are typically given a preliminary rating as part of assigned reviewers’ initial evaluations; an application’s final rating or 'overall impact score' is determined by the entire review panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare preliminary evaluations and be ready to justify and adjust scores during the SRG discussion; consult NIH scoring guidance (e.g., 'Scoring in First Level Peer Review') for numeric scoring conventions and panel procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing reviewer critiques (summary statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer critiques are part of the summary statement and an important source of feedback for what reviewers liked and didn’t like about their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clear, constructive critiques that explain strengths and weaknesses; use provided NIH reviewer critique guidance and submit/manage critiques through IAR so they become part of the applicant-facing summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to certify that they understand the rules of integrity and confidentiality in the peer review process and the consequences for not following these rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certify understanding of confidentiality rules, protect application materials, and comply with NIH policies; certification is required before meetings and may be tracked via IAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and declare conflicts of interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must certify before and after review meetings that all conflicts of interest (COI) were identified and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any real or perceived conflicts promptly, follow NIH COI management procedures during meetings, and use IAR to certify pre‑meeting and post‑meeting COI forms as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reviewer trainings (integrity and bias awareness)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH reviewers are required to take trainings in review integrity and bias awareness to participate in most NIH review meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete mandated trainings (e.g., Review Integrity and Bias Awareness Training) prior to participating in meetings; these trainings cover expectations for impartiality and confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Internet Assisted Review (IAR) system
rubrics_metrics.description: IAR is a web‑based module within NIH’s eRA Systems that is used by reviewers to view meeting materials, certify their confidentiality and COI forms, access applications and submit scores and critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform reviewer tasks in IAR such as accessing meeting materials, filling out personal profile, certifying pre‑meeting COI, submitting/managing critiques and scores, viewing other reviewers’ critiques, and certifying post‑meeting COI; consult IAR help resources for navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑level peer review approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for the NIH to award research funds, an application must be approved by two levels of NIH peer review (as stipulated in CFR 52h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that first‑level peer review (SRG) assesses scientific/technical merit (including overall impact) and that a second level of review is also required for funding decisions; coordinate evaluations accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow meeting roles and SRG procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are brought together as a Scientific Review Group (SRG) to discuss the merits of the studies proposed in individual applications and submit a final impact score for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be familiar with meeting overview and roles (e.g., assigned reviewers, discussant responsibilities), observe discussion etiquette, and consider watching mock study section videos to learn how reviewers discuss applications.
